lead: A hillside neighbourhood between the Ronda de Dalt and Collserola, of houses with gardens and family life.
text: It climbs from the Ronda de Dalt towards Collserola and mixes the old centre of Sant Gervasi de Cassoles, an independent municipality until 1897, with areas of houses with gardens and low-rise residential buildings. It was an autonomous municipality from 1714 until its annexation in 1897, and it keeps the Jardins de la Tamarita, designed by Rubió i Tudurí in 1918 and opened as a public park in 1994, as well as La Rotonda, the Frare Blanc and Gaudí's Bellesguard.

It is an area of family housing, with schools, gardens and good connections to the Diagonal and the ring roads, and with the CosmoCaixa museum a few minutes away. At 11,997 inhabitants/km², it is much less dense than Sant Gervasi-Galvany or El Putxet, and that shows in the pace of the street. If you are selling, the average sale price (5,438 €/m² in 2025) is practically in line with the Sarrià-Sant Gervasi average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 435,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Sarrià-Sant Gervasi (4th of 6 by price). If you are investing, the average rent (1,659 €/month) is in line with the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Houses with gardens and low-rise residential buildings, on sloping streets.
